subject: R-2.11.1 macro problem + RApacheInfo test not working.

messages.author: 596788cb1219e353
messages.subject: R-2.11.1 macro problem + RApacheInfo test not working.
parts:
Just starting: two or three problems have been discovered so far.

(1) R-2.11.1 hides at least one symbol required by RApache.
(2) The quick install for Debian/Ubuntu mentioned at
http://biostat.mc.vanderbilt.edu/rapache/manual.html
does not install on Ubuntu 10.04. The problem is that
the build requires a static library: libuuid.a, that is missing.
There is a bug in Ubuntu-space for this.
(3) RApacheInfo is not working. This is probably an error in my
configuration.

I took copious notes.

$ uname -a
Linux ceshannon 2.6.32-25-generic #44-Ubuntu SMP Fri Sep 17 20:05:27
UTC 2010 x86_64 GNU/Linux
$ hostname -f
ceshannon.dlinkddns.com

RApache was built from subversion source. Revision #451.

Build and install R
===================

Download the source. Packages and downloads are not compiled in a
manner that exposes R as a library. If you start up rapache without
doing this, you may see an error message indicating that getConnection
is not a symbol. The critical step is the "--enable-R-shlib" step
done when configuring your build environment.

% unset R_HOME
# configure --enable-R-shlib
# make
# make check
# make dvi
# make pdf
# make info
# make install
# make install-dvi
# make install-info
# make install-pdf

Build and install RApache
=========================

Build rapache

# unset R_HOME
# configure --with-apache2-apxs=/usr/bin/apxs2 --with-R=/usr/local/
lib64/R/bin/R \
--with-apreq2-config=/usr/bin/apreq2-config
# make
# sudo make install


Configure Apache
================
1. Change DefaultType in /etc/apache2/apache2.conf

DefaultType text/html

2. Create a file libR.conf in /etc/ld.so.conf.d. The
content should contain the directory containing libR.so.

# cat /etc/ld.so.conf.d/libR.so
# libR default configuration
/usr/local/lib64/R/lib

(Changing file /etc/apache2/envvars by adding an entry that sets
LD_LIBRARY_PATH might be a cleaner solution).


3. Add to the end of apache2.conf

LoadModule R_module /usr/lib/apache2/modules/mod_R.so
<Location /RApacheInfo>
SetHandler r-info
</Location>

# apache2ctl start
apache2: Syntax error on line 238 of /etc/apache2/apache2.conf: \
Cannot load /usr/lib/apache2/modules/mod_R.so into server: \
/usr/lib/apache2/modules/mod_R.so: undefined symbol: getConnection

Uninstall Rapache and R
=======================

There is no uninstall in the Makefile for rapache.

# rm /usr/lib/apache2/modules/mod_R.so
# rm -rf /usr/local/lib64/R/library/RApache
# rm -rf /usr/local/lib64/R/library/Rserve

Go back to the R source code directory.

# make uninstall

Change R Source Code
====================
Comment out line 120 in the code src/main/connections.c so that
getConnection(int n)
is no longer proceeded with an "attribute_hidden" macro.

//attribute_hidden
Rconnection getConnection(int n)

Recompile and reinstall R.

Reinstall Rapache

Check the Apache configuration
# apache2ctl -t -D DUMP_MODULES
core_module (static)
...
R_module (shared)
Syntax OK

# apache2ctl start
#

Navigate to http://ceshannon.dlinkddns.com/RApacheInfo.

Nothing shows up. The tail of /var/log/apache2/error.log reads

[Tue Sep 28 16:47:38 2010] [error] [client 192.168.0.197] File does
not exist: /var/www/RApacheInfo

192.168.0.197 is the correct LAN IP address. I'm going to check for
external visibility of by Dynamic DNS site right now.

messages.subject: Re: R-2.11.1 macro problem + RApacheInfo test not working.
parts:
Hi Allan,

Nice work on installing everything from source!

On Sep 28, 7:20 pm, Allan Jacobs <jacobsallans...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Just starting: two or three problems have been discovered so far.
>
> (1) R-2.11.1 hides at least one symbol required by RApache.

You're attempting to install an old version of rApache. If you checked
out the entire rApache svn repository, the latest version is in the
branches/rapache-1-1-branch folder. Or you can just get the latest
tarball here:

http://www.rapache.net/downloads.html

This should fix (3) as well.

> (2) The quick install for Debian/Ubuntu mentioned at
>    http://biostat.mc.vanderbilt.edu/rapache/manual.html
>     does not install on Ubuntu 10.04.  The problem is that
>     the build requires a static library: libuuid.a, that is missing.
>     There is a bug in Ubuntu-space for this.

Yes, this is an unfortunate situation as the recommended version of
libapreq2-dev for Ubuntu 10.4 contains a reference to the missing
libuuid.a file. If you scope out the debian directory under
rapache-1-1-branch in the rApache subversion repository, you'll see
that I address that in the rules file. I follow these steps to
configure and build rapache:

./configure --with-R=/usr/bin/R --with-apache2-apxs=/usr/bin/apxs2
--with-apreq2-config=/usr/bin/apreq2-config
if test -f /usr/bin/lsb_release -a `/usr/bin/lsb_release -cs` =
"lucid"; then \
cp /usr/lib/libapreq2.la libapreq2.la~; \
sed -e "s/\/usr\/lib\/libuuid.la/-luuid/g;s/libdir='\/lib/
libdir='\/usr\/lib/g" < libapreq2.la~ > libapreq2.la; \
fi;

Execute that and then make, make install. If you can't get it to work,
try uninstalling the libapreq2* debian packages and just allow
configure to build with the bundled version.

Jeff
